findings.conclusion: Drela eq185 and user guide define Lift as integrated aerodynamic lift+drag projected on [-sin(global alpha),0,cos(global alpha)]. This is exactly the current and integrated08 projection. It is neither body Fz nor local normal force, gravity/support reaction, one-tip load, nor Trefftz CLi.

All27 accepted curve points have force=surface_force=distributed_aero_force, with zero apparent, body, engine, circulation-rate and point-drag vectors. Both aerodynamic-only half-wrench sums reproduce the total force. Gravity added inside wrenches.py changes internal Mc traces only; it is never added to Lift.

Associated model specifies L1m,T1s,F1N, so documented dimensional Lift is N. Reference area.5222 affects CL normalization but is absent from the dimensional force projection. Producer model bytes/output unit overrides remain unproved; numerical frequency/force agreement cannot establish them.

All17 Flare30 MATLAB plotted incidence values differ from the Flare30 script requests because Analysis.m plots Var5 of experimental CSV against ASW output rows. Current curve contract uses requested script alpha exactly and does not repeat that plotting defect. At row17 labels29.865099784437803 versus requested30.26388985466935.

alpha[2] is the port sensor full local incidence including induced velocity, not global requested alpha. Phi[2] is port Euler bank, not physical hinge fold. Neither should replace global alpha in the Lift projection. Associated model has aligned initial sensor V=x,A=z.

!V22 specifies indicated speed; !A specifies constraint parameters rather than printing achieved states. Script sets anchored defaults only after constructing point17, with no all-point P command. Startup auto-loaded .set/.pnt/.con, actual density/altitude, attitude/gravity, load factor, controls, PG/stall/F settings, exact mesh/modes and executable bytes are absent. Script path names5.92 but does not pin that executable or establish equivalence to the public documentation edition.

At high-incidence row17 the force magnitude20.58616811949394N is already less than archived Lift20.7534N. No rigid unit-axis change applied only to the same saved force can close the entire gap. The known plot-alpha projection change is only+.03614804499493829N, without rerunning any physics.

formula_checks.result: rho*Gamma*(V_hv cross s)*ds. V_hv includes induced flow; span-normal magnitude is not substituted for the vector. No additional ad hoc cosine/sweep multiplier is justified.

Full-velocity friction plus span-normal pressure drag plus 2*rho*(Vperp/|Vperp|)*(Vcp dot ncp)^2*c, integrated over ds. Literal Cdf=Cdp=0 removes the first two terms but not nonlinear leakage drag. Dropping the third term would change the published model.
cl=2*Gamma/(normal chord*|Vperp_hv|); residual subtracts |Vperp|/dCLda*Ks*fstall. dCLda=4*pi*h. Smooth activation uses both CL limits and width. These are not global CL or projected f_aero.

ASW chord is beam-normal chord; the input slope determines wind-directed collocation. Dynamic sweep is already present through section geometry, perpendicular velocity and vector force. The source should not multiply this normal chord by another cosine.

Surface circulation plus profile force is projected on [-sin(global alpha),0,cos(global alpha)]. Body Fz and sensor-local alpha are different outputs. Global CL uses total force; the specified-Lift operating constraint uses surface force excluding apparent mass. This generic scope difference is inactive for the saved stationary FFWT state.

Quarter-chord-to-axis arm uses circulatory force; local Cm receives the section-normal Mach factor. Profile moment is zero in this theory. Literal Cm=0 and zero rates avoid unsteady closure questions.

Sensor alpha uses posed sensor axes and local airflow; bank is sensor Euler bank. Neither replaces global Lift projection. output_fields/rom_outputs preserve or derive their stated outputs; they do not supply an alternative stationary archived Lift formula.
